To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the assembly of the C membrane attack complex on the cell surface of C-sensitive Escherichia cells results in inhibition of the inner membrane, and that this inhibition can be measured by the decrease in oxygen consumption by these cells.
complement-resistant strains of Eschericha coli are inhibited by C attack, and the mechanism of this inhibition is damage to some component or components of the respiring, inner membrane.

complement-resistant Eschericia coli are inhibited in function by complement attack, that the mechanism of inhibition involves the assembly of a C membrane attack complex, and that the inhibition of inner membrane functions may be one mechanism of cellular resistance to complement attack.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of mechanisms involved in the inhibition of function in bacteria under complement attack, and the role of this process in the killing of complement-sensitive cells.
the mechanisms of complement-mediated inhibition of function of the inner membrane in C-sensitive and C-resistant Escherichiae coli.
the study of the mechanisms by which complement kills gram-negative bacteria and with the mechanisms of cellular resistance to complement attack.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
C-sensitive cells are killed by a mechanism involving the formation of the MAC on the outer membrane and the subsequent inhibition of inner-membrane function.
the MAC is the critical effector of complement-mediated killing of bacteria.
C-resistant cells have evolved to resist C attack by a variety of means.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assembly of the C membrane attack complex is sufficient for the inhibition of cellular function in C-sensitive cells.
C-mediated inhibition of bacterial function is a general phenomenon in C-sensitive strains.

C-sensitive cells are killed by a mechanism involving inhibition of inner membrane functions by MAC, whereas C-resistant strains are inhibited by MAC but are capable of recovering from the effects of the MAC, perhaps through the action of a C-sensitive factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complement system is a powerful and versatile effector system that can be used to target specific cell populations for destruction.
the complement system is an important part of the immune system and is used to kill pathogens.
C-mediated damage to the inner membrane is a critical component of C-mediated killing, and that this damage is reversible in C-resistant strains of Escherchia coli.
